articles.title: Josh Pate decries college football ‘leadership’ for using playoff expansion as ‘a bailout’
articles.summary: On Tuesday, Front Office Sports’s Ryan Glasspiegel opened his Tuned In panel with John Fanta and Josh Pate by asking Pate for his thoughts on an expanded Col...
articles.body:
On Tuesday, Front Office Sports's Ryan Glasspiegel opened his Tuned In panel with John Fanta and Josh Pate by asking Pate for his thoughts on an expanded College Football Playoff.

"Hate it," Pate, who now hosts a weekly college football show on ESPN, said. "Viscerally hate it."

Elsewhere Tuesday, Ross Dellenger reported that ESPN and the College Football Playoff are "close" to a deal on an expanded 24-team field. Pate, however, shouted his opposition from the rooftops at the Front Office Sports conference in New York City.

Pate laid out that the transfer portal and NIL may have caused expanding to a 12-team playoff, which he also opposed, to retroactively seem like the right decision. But the regular season — "the most valuable commodity that college football has" — has been subsequently harmed, as urgency is diluted when top contenders clash in the regular season in favor of "a safety net" and "manufactured urgency on games featuring teams playing for a 22-seed."

Later, Pate delved even deeper into his personal gripes with the notion of a 24-team playoff.

"When you went from BCS to four-team, there was supermajority public support behind it. When you went from four to 12, there was supermajority public support behind it. And one of the most disingenuous things, maybe even just one of the flat-out most ignorant approaches that I've seen over the past year is — I hesitate to call them leaders, but the movers in college football even going so far as to acknowledge publicly, 'Well, we know that fan sentiment is against this.'

"But it's almost like, 'Well, you'll watch anyway. You'll take what we give you anyway. But in the aggregate, we've really screwed this up nine ways from Sunday. We need a bailout. We've gotta create revenue somewhere, so we're gonna call it an expanded playoff. Really, what it is is it's an ATM to bail out very bad decision-making from, and I use this term loosely, leadership in college football."

As we've seen with college football in recent years — or with the NFL and its increasing international slate — financial incentives often supersede what's best for the health of the sport.

Unfortunately, even if Pate and college football fans hate it, people will still watch an expanded College Football Playoff, even if begrudgingly, validating the decision-makers in college football in taking viewership for granted in spite of a diluted product.

articles.title: Cincinnati Bengals: Bye comes at a good time for recovery, self-reflection
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals coach Zac Taylor initially didn’t like the idea of a bye so early in the season, but as it turns out, the Week 6 timing isn’t so bad. The...
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals coach Zac Taylor initially didn't like the idea of a bye so early in the season, but as it turns out, the Week 6 timing isn't so bad.

The Bengals had several injuries to key players pop up the last few weeks, and now is a good time to recover after the hottest game they'll play all season.

Coming off a 31-24 win at Miami on Sunday, Oct. 11, in 90-degree temperatures, they are 3-2 going into a bye before a big AFC North matchup at first-place Baltimore (4-1) on Oct. 25. Cincinnati is in a three-way tie with the rest of the division.

"Here we are through five weeks, and we got a tremendous opportunity coming out of the bye with the divisional game to put ourselves to the top there, and so it's right in front of us," Taylor said Monday. "So, opportunity to get healthy, get your legs back under us. I do think the bye hits really well playing after Miami. I mean, I coached there for four years, never really thought about that, but the heat really does drain you to where I'm sure it affects you the next week. So, I'm happy that it hit for our guys to be able to recover and get that, and then get your legs back under us and start getting ready for some colder weather, which we're very familiar with as the season gets going here."

Both Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin/neck) were back from Week 4 injuries, and Bryan Cook returned after missing one game due to an ankle injury that occurred in Week 3 at Pittsburgh, but the time off now will allow them to heal further.

Right guard Dalton Risner also has been playing through discomfort in his knee, and safety Kyle Dugger, who has missed the last two games, remains week-to-week with a quadriceps injury.

Cincinnati also is taking a look at a pec injury for tight end Tanner Hudson, but Taylor did not have any further information on how serious that is. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman is going on injured reserve with a broken forearm, which he suffered on a special teams play late in the game Sunday.

"I think that was your gut reaction when you first saw when the bye was, 'Man,'" Taylor said. "You kind of like it more towards Thanksgiving, but I do think just where our team is right now and the way that these last three games have gone down to the wire and guys playing through some stuff right now, it is a good time to get the bye and get our legs back underneath us, get some guys healthy, and go full force when we come back from Baltimore."

The Bengals were pleased to get the win and be back above .500 before the bye, but they left Sunday's game not feeling satisfied. After reviewing the film, Taylor still had some of the same feelings as he did right after the game. Cincinnati pulled ahead 28-10 on Ja'Marr Chase's 45-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter and let Miami back into it.

Although the win never felt in doubt, the Bengals had a chance to end the game there and instead made some unforced errors — like penalties or stepping out of bounds on a punt return — that allowed the Dolphins to rally.

"I just think there's that moment there where it's 28-10 in the fourth quarter, and that's where we got to end the game, you know, and get the ball back, go down and score, get to 35-10 and kind of finish it up that way and call it a day," Taylor said. "And then instead, you know, in all phases, we weren't enough to be able to finish it like that, made it interesting."

"But I do think if you really just look at the tape … there's a lot of moments where all the units played really well and did some really good things to build on, and so coming out of Week 5, I think we recognize some things that we're doing really well, and then there's a couple things that are really easy to clean up, really easy. So the good news is it's not a concern that 'oh man, this is unfixable.' It's just a couple things that we gotta get cleaned up going into the next divisional game."

Through five games, Taylor still sees a team that could be pretty special. However, the Bengals have to clean up penalties and turnovers, especially in the red zone, prevent explosives in the run defense, and be more explosive in their own running game to achieve their goals of reaching the playoffs and being a Super Bowl contender.

Cincinnati is ranked 10th in points scored and 11th in points allowed through Week 5, before Monday Night Football. All phases can be better, but there's especially belief the offense hasn't yet hit its stride.

"We talked with the guys about two things can be true at the same time," offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said. "You can make enough plays in any given week to win, which we did (Sunday), and you could still be self-critical and understand that I think the best version of this offense is ahead of us and we have work to do to get there. So happy with some of the improvements we made from the week prior, and we just got to keep moving in the right direction."

articles.title: Mallory Swanson scores late equalizer as USWNT rallies from 2 goals down to draw Spain, 2-2
articles.summary: The USWNT trailed Spain by two goals for the second straight match, but this time Ashley Sanchez and Mallory Swanson led a second-half comeback.
articles.body:
CHESTER, Pa. — Eight months from now, when the U.S. and Spain arrive in Brazil among the elites aiming to hoist the World Cup trophy, these autumn friendlies between FIFA's top-ranked women's soccer teams are going to be a distant memory.

But in the moment, with the global tournament on the horizon and the No. 1 and No. 2 titans seeking an upper hand, two clashes three days and 120 miles apart showed Spanish excellence and American resilience.

Facing another two-goal halftime deficit Tuesday, the U.S. answered with two of their own, including Mallory Swanson's sensational finish in the 86th minute for a 2-2 draw in front of 18,648 at Subaru Park.

Swanson, who on Saturday returned from more than two years away to give birth to her first child, was a second-half sub again. After threatening to tie the game in the 69th, she did it in dramatic fashion.

Michelle Cooper laid off the ball to Swanson, who turned, lifted the ball to herself and whacked a 16-yard shot into the left corner for her first goal since the Olympic gold-medal winner against Brazil in Paris.

Ashley Sanchez scored in the 49th minute for the U.S.

Friendlies are largely without consequence, but this was a learning stretch for Emma Hayes and the No. 2 Americans, who, coupled with the 2-0 setback Saturday in Washington , were in danger of losing consecutive matches for the first time since a three-game skid in 2022 and dropping back-to-back home games for the first time since 2017.

Before Spain's visit, the U.S. had gone 11-0-6 all time in matchups between the top two teams in the world.

After a promising start Tuesday, it fell apart for the U.S. in a five-minute span with glaring errors against the unforgiving opponents.

In its past 29 matches, Spain has lost twice in regular time, both to European champion England.

The Americans will now turn attention to the CONCACAF W Championship starting Nov. 27 in the Dallas suburb of Mansfield, Texas, and culminating Dec. 5 in Houston.

With a quarterfinal victory over 78th-ranked El Salvador, the Americans would qualify for their 10th consecutive World Cup. Even with a seismic upset, they could still advance through a playoff.

Spain is among 18 teams to have already qualified for the 32-nation competition. Spain and the U.S. will be seeded teams in the Dec. 11 draw in Rio de Janeiro.

Hayes made four lineup changes, adding goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce, left back Gisele Thompson, midfielder Claire Hutton and Sanchez, the National Women's Soccer League top scorer whose previous start was almost two years ago.

They replaced Claudia Dickey, Avery Patterson, Lily Yohannes and Alyssa Thompson, respectively.

Spain coach Sonia Bermúdez named six new starters, including Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez, Barcelona defender Irene Paredes and multiple young players.

Unlike the first meeting, the Americans crackled from the start with creativity, confidence, energy and vision. They didn't parlay it into a serious threat, however.

Tullis-Joyce was tested in the 14th minute, blocking Clara Pinedo's rising 12-yarder after the Spanish attacker made a clean run into space to collect a through ball.

Spain had found its rhythm, and in the 27th minute, La Roja went ahead on Alexia Putellas' tap-in.

Clara Serrajordi received the ball at the top corner of the penalty area after Tierna Davidson had left her. To make matters worse, Sanchez had failed to drop back and help.

Serrajordi sent a low cross that Pinedo dummied by letting the ball pass between her legs. Having made a run through a central channel, Putellas touched the ball into the net from the door step.

Five minutes later, it only got worse. Pinedo intercepted Tullis-Joyce's aimless clearance and delivered a through ball targeting Salma Paralluelo. Davidson took a bad angle, allowing the Spanish forward to get behind her and drill a 12-yard shot off the underside of the crossbar and into the net.

U.S. forays the rest of the half had a feel of desperation instead of connection. Rodríguez wasn't bothered.

Three minutes into the second half, though, the deficit was halved. Breaking out of its end, the U.S. supplied Sanchez in space. She took the initiative, dribbling into the box and taking on Ona Batlle before placing an angled shot into the far lower corner — her first international goal since July 2022.

Hayes turned to her bench in a big way in the 61st minute, making five changes, including Swanson's arrival and Trinity Rodman's departure.

Swanson threatened to tie it in the 69th, collecting Yohannes' wonderful one-touch pass behind the defense and forcing a quality save by Rodríguez.

The U.S. continued pressing for the equalizer, manufacturing several threats in the run of play and off set pieces. Spain was under duress.

Finally, Swanson struck, setting off celebrations on the field and in the stands, where her husband, Chicago Cubs star Dansby Swanson, watched with pride.

Yohannes almost won it deep in stoppage time with a shot through traffic that was tipped away spectacularly by Rodríguez.

U.S. notes : Defender Kate Del Fava and forward Pietra Tordin made their international debuts in the 80th minute.

images.caption: Mallory Swanson scored a sensational 86th-minute equalizer Tuesday to complete the USWNT's comeback from a two-goal deficit against No. 1 Spain. (Georgia Soares/USSF via Getty Images)

articles.title: USWNT vs. Spain Score, Highlights, Stats and Reaction
articles.summary: The United States women's national team didn't want a repeat of Saturday's 2-0 loss against Spain on Tuesday night. It took a pretty epic second half to avoid some unwanted déjà vu.
articles.body:
The United States women's national team didn't want a repeat of Saturday's 2-0 loss against Spain on Tuesday night. It took a pretty epic second half to avoid some unwanted déjà vu.

The USWNT erased a 2-0 deficit against the defending World Cup Champions and salvaged a 2-2 draw after a fantastic second half performance.

Spain took the lead in the first half behind goals from two-time Ballon d'Or Féminin-winner Alexia Putellas and Salma Paralluelo.

Putellas was a monster in the first half, also finishing with an assist, and easily could have had a second.

But the United States came roaring back behind goals from Ashley Sanchez and Mallory Swanson.

Spain finished the match holding 56 percent of possession but it was the Americans who led in overall shots (15-12), shots on goal (6-5) and corners (8-5). The United States were downright dominant at points in the second half.

Overall, USWNT supporters were happy with the showing:

The game played out quite differently from what head coach Emma Hayes said she wanted, however, at least in the first half.

"My big request to the team is to do it earlier," she told reporters prior to the rematch. "Like, start earlier with the things that really matter."

Instead, the game fell into a similar cadence—Spain were far better earlier but the United States slowly seized control of the game. This time, however, a strong second-half showing also resulted in goals.

"I think we're much closer to them than we were three years ago, definitely," Hayes told reporters following Saturday's rematch.

Tuesday's effort should only reinforce that belief.

articles.title: Mallory Swanson nets first goal since Olympics as USWNT draws 2-2 with Spain
articles.summary: Ashley Sanchez also scored early in the second half for the U.S. after first-half goals from Alexia Putellas and Salma Paralluelo gave Spain a 2-0 lead.
articles.body: CHESTER, Pa. — Mallory Swanson scored her first goal since the gold medal match at the 2024 Olympics in the 86th minute to pull the United States into a 2-2 draw with Spain on Tuesday night. Ashley Sanchez also scored early in the second half for the United States after first-half goals from Alexia Putellas and Salma Paralluelo gave Spain a 2-0 lead. “I mean, this mentality of this team has always been you stay with it,” said Swanson, who subbed into the game in the second half. “That's what this crest means.” It was the second of two friendly matches against Spain, the 2023 Women's World Cup winners. Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro scored in the first 14 minutes to lift Spain to a 2-0 victory in the first match Saturday in Washington. Spain, ranked No. 1 in the world, has already qualified for the World Cup next summer in Brazil. The United States was using the matches as preparation for World Cup qualifying later this year. Putellas, the two-time Ballon d'Or winner, was making her 150th appearance for Spain. She put Spain in front in the 27th minute with her 43rd international goal, a tap-in at the far post off a feed from Clara Pinedo. Some five minutes later, U.S. goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce misplayed the ball up the field and Spain pounced. Putellas sent the ball forward to Paralluelo, whose blast hit the crossbar and fell into the goal to make it 2-0. It was the first time the United States has given up two first-half goals to an opponent in consecutive matches since 2011. The U.S. pulled back a goal early in the second when Sanchez found a gap and scored to the far post. Sanchez was making her first start for the U.S. since Oct. 30, 2024, against Argentina. Sanchez has been on a tear for the North Carolina Courage in the National Women’s Soccer League, scoring a league-leading 20 goals in 27 games. In the final minutes, Michelle Cooper took a long ball from Kate Del Fava and sent it over to Swanson for the volley. Swanson's last goal gave the United States a 1-0 victory over Brazil at the Paris Games. She spent 2025 on maternity leave for the birth of her daughter. “I think one of our big things in the game plan was just like finding those spaces in the box and being clinical in the box, and you could see that,” Swanson said. Lily Yohannes nearly scored for the United States in stoppage time, but Misa Rodríguez made a diving save. “Obviously, we always want to win, that's the type of team that we are, and I think if we had 20 more minutes we definitely probably would have won,” Sanchez said. “But it was good just to get a tie against a team like that and come back from 2-nil down.” Spain dominated despite missing some of its biggest players, including Aitana Bonmatí, who is still working her way back from a broken leg. Vicky López, Mariona Caldentey and goalkeeper Cata Coll were all also unavailable for the matches because of injuries. Chicago Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson, Mallory Swanson's husband, and tennis player Ben Shelton, who is dating Trinity Rodman, were among those in the crowd at Subaru Park.

articles.standfirst: "Bueno... Ha sido efectiva al final. Lo llamaría la casi rabona, pero no sé... en el momento me ha salido así. Ha salido bien para la asistencia de Gordon"
articles.summary: "Bueno... Ha sido efectiva al final. Lo llamaría la casi rabona, pero no sé... en el momento me ha salido así. Ha salido bien para la asistencia de Gordon"
articles.body: Lamine Yamal explicó su espectacular regate a Elmali para asistir a Gordon en el 1-3 en el partido de Champions League que el F.C. Barcelona ganó 1-4 al Galatasaray. "Bueno... Ha sido efectiva al final. Lo llamaría la casi rabona, pero no sé... en el momento me ha salido así. Ha salido bien para la asistencia de Gordon", explicó el futbolista español en la cámaras de Movistar Plus Deportes. Su compañero Fermín destacó tras el partido que "Lamine es un amigo y un gran compañero. Cuando la tiene él, siempre busco el desmarque porque sé que me busca y me ve. Es el mejor del mundo, tiene mucha calidad, nos llevamos bien fuera del campo y dentro del campo eso se transmite también". Lamine Yamal, que fue nombrado el Mejor Jugador del Partido, estuvo acompañado en el estadio Ali Sami Yen Sports Complex RAMS Park de Estambul por su madre (Sheila Ebana) y por su novia, la conocida creadora de contenido Inés García. Hansi Flick, entrenador del Barcelona, elogió el buen partido de Lamine Yamal, clave en el segundo tiempo con dos asistencias a Fermín y a Gordon. "Lamine Yamal ha hecho una gran segunda parte y para nosotros ha sido muy importante. Ha sido fantástico como ha dominado el juego" apuntó el técnico alemán. Flick subrayó que "Lamine Yamal está muy bien físicamente y disfruta jugando al fútbol, como hemos visto en el segundo tiempo. Es especial tener a un jugador así a este nivel y que cambia los partidos de esta manera".

articles.title: Pietro Falcetta, el 'fantasista' que amenaza al príncipe de Europa
articles.standfirst: El italo-brasileño es una de las estrellas de la Roma Primavera y hoy se miden al Real Madrid, vigente campeón
articles.summary: El italo-brasileño es una de las estrellas de la Roma Primavera y hoy se miden al Real Madrid, vigente campeón
articles.body: Este próximo miércoles, a las 14.00 horas en el Tre Fontane romano, el Real Madrid, campeón de la UEFA Youth League, se medirá a una de las mejores canteras de Italia: la de la Roma. Allí, un talento emerge a sus 18 años: Pietro Teixeira Falcetta, nacido en Valdagno, Vicenza, pero internacional sub-17 con Brasil, es una de las joyas de Trigoria. La Roma dejó clara su categoría en Estambul, hace ya unas cuantas semanas. Tras la roja a Satik, remontaron un 2-0 en contra para acabar ganando 2-4 en Turquía en la primera fecha de la Youth League. En ese contexto, Pietro brilló con dos asistencias y el gol que cerró el triunfo italiano. Es la primera temporada del '10' en el equipo Sub19 de la Roma después de haber destacado el pasado curso en la categoría Sub18 italiana con 16 goles y 10 asistencias. En categoría Primavera, la máxima división del fútbol juvenil italiano, ya suma goles y asistencias para colocar a 'La Loba' en tercera posición. Falcetta, que debutó con la Sub17 de Brasil el pasado 2025, ya ha entrenado con el primer equipo de Gian Piero Gasperini en numerosas ocasiones. Su futuro en Italia, sin embargo, está en el aire: su contrato con la Roma expira el próximo 30 de junio y aún no ha renovado. Este 'fantasista' pequeñito y 'jugón' encarna a la perfección lo que representa un '10' de la vieja escuela. Un enganche zurdo, muy técnico y con una gran creatividad y visión de juego. Un talento de la prolífica cantera de Trigoria que se presenta como la gran amenaza para el Real Madrid de Álvaro López.

articles.title: El 'villano' Asensio se reencuentra con Emery: "Cuida cada detalle y es muy cercano"
articles.standfirst: El mediapunta balear, que militó en el Aston Villa durante la segunda mitad de la temporada 24-25, regresó el pasado fin de semana con Fenerbahçe
articles.summary: El mediapunta balear, que militó en el Aston Villa durante la segunda mitad de la temporada 24-25, regresó el pasado fin de semana con Fenerbahçe
articles.body: "Unai (Emery) es un entrenador que conozco desde hace tiempo. Ha sido clave para que pueda venir aquí. Su idea me sienta perfectamente", reconoció Marco Asensio en su presentación con el Aston Villa en enero de 2025. Año y medio después, ahora en las filas de Fenerbahçe, regresa a Birmingham para medirse a los 'villanos'. Asensio no pasaba por un buen momento por aquel entonces. Luis Enrique le había 'borrado' de sus planes en el PSG y no dudó en buscar una salida en el mercado invernal de la temporada 24-25. El destino, siempre caprichoso, enfrentó al Aston Villa y el conjunto parisino en los cuartos de final de aquella edición de la Champions. En total, disputó 21 partidos en los que marcó ocho goles y repartió una asistencia. Sin embargo, las limitaciones del Aston Villa para operar en el mercado por sus restricciones en el 'Fair Play' impidieron que pudiese quedarse en Villa Park de forma permanente una vez terminada la cesión. "Pensaba que iba a acabar aquí. Era el objetivo... pero, al final, no ocurrió. Principalmente, por razones financieras. El PSG estaba siendo más duro con nosotros", explicó Monchi en una entrevista con 'El Desmarque'. "Marco (Asensio) también estaba nervioso porque el mercado avanzaba y el trato no se cerraba". Esperó hasta el final. Pero, a horas de cerrar el mercado, Asensio acabó aceptando la propuesta de Fenerbahçe... a pesar de haber caído en la última ronda previa de clasificación a la Champions 25-26. Asensio, en cualquier caso, siempre ha tenido palabras de agradecimiento hacia Emery por 'rescatarlo' cuando no contaba para el PSG. "Es un entrenador increíble. Cuida cada detalle y, en lo personal, es muy cercano con los jugadores", contaba unos meses atrás en MARCA. "Tuvimos una segunda parte de temporada espectacular, ganando casi todos los partidos en la Premier, en Copa llegando a disputar las semifinales en Wembley y en Champions estuvimos a punto de pasar". Explicaba, también, por qué decidió continuar su carrera en Turquía. "En el PSG también tuve momentos felices. Pero lo que buscaba aquí era tener continuidad porque es lo que te lleva a tu mejor nivel. Creo que lo conseguí en el Aston Villa la temporada pasada, donde también fui muy feliz". Asensio, desde luego, volvió a reecontrarse consigo mismo en las filas de un Fenerbahçe que no se quedó lejos de destronar a Galatasaray. Mucha culpa tuvieron sus 13 goles y 14 asistencias entre todas las competiciones. Lamine Yamal, de hecho, fue el único jugador español que generó más goles (28) el curso pasado. Jugadores españoles con más goles generados la temporada pasada: Esta temporada heredó el '10' de un Fenerbahçe que le rodeó de socios como Greenwood, Muriqi o Lukaku para, casi 20 años después, regresar a la Liga de Campeones. Arrancó con asistencia ante el Sturm Graz en las rondas previas y un gol ante el Konyaspor a final de agosto. Aquel día, por desgracia, sufrió una lesión que le ha tenido fuera de los terrenos durante más de un mes. Durante este período, además de perderse el estreno en Champions ante la Roma, tuvo que salir a desmentir unas informaciones que circulaban en Turquía sobre la necesidad de tener que pasar por quirófano. Tanto es así que, antes del parón, ya estuvo presente en el banquillo contra Eyüspor... y reapareció con gol el pasado fin de semana para iniciar la victoria contra Rizespor. "Estoy contento por el gol y la victoria. Tenemos que continuar de esta manera. Claro que creo que iré ganando ritmo partido a partido. Fue un período difícil para mí, pero pienso que, poco a poco, llegaré a punto mucho mejor", dijo después del partido un Marco Asensio que, esta noche, tratará de ser el 'villano' de Birmingham.

articles.title: Choque de jeques entre City y PSG
articles.standfirst: Luis Enrique se reencuentra con un Enzo Maresca que, a los mandos del Chelsea, le derrotó en la final del Mundial de clubes 2025
articles.summary: Luis Enrique se reencuentra con un Enzo Maresca que, a los mandos del Chelsea, le derrotó en la final del Mundial de clubes 2025
articles.body: Manchester City y PSG son los clubes que mejor encarnan el ascenso de los 'nuevos ricos' en el fútbol europeo. Son , de hecho, dos de los tres clubes que han estrenado su palmarés en Champions a lo largo de este siglo... gracias al impulso generado por la llegada del dinero procedente de Emiratos Árabes Unidos y Qatar, respectivamente, a la planta noble del Etihad Stadium y el Parque de los Príncipes. Esta noche, ambos se miden en un City of Manchester que recibirá a su equipo por primera vez desde que la Premier le declaró culpable de infringir 114 de los 115 cargos que se le atribuyen por esquivar las normas financieras entre las temporadas 08-09 y la 2017-18. "Sólo estoy concentrado en mañana", reconoció un Enzo Maresca al ser preguntado sobre la posibilidad de que esta fuese la última temporada del City en Champions. "Vamos a intentar mejorar en comparación a los últimos años, en los que el club tuvo dificultades en Champions", insistía un Enzo Maresca que se estrenó con victoria en Do Dragao en Champions y viene con la moral reforzada tras la goleada lograda en Anfield el pasado fin de semana para alargar su pleno de victorias (6/6) en Premier. La temporada pasada se estrenó en Liga de Campeones a los mandos de un Chelsea con el que cosechó un balance de cuatro victorias, un empate y dos derrotas durante la fase liga. Sabe, eso sí, lo que es levantar la 'Orejona', ya que ejerció como asistente de Pep Guardiola, que estará presente esta noche en el Etihad, en la campaña 23-24. "Es una sensación agradable. Especialmente para él, porque esta ha sido su casa durante 10 años. Sigue siendo su casa por todo lo que ha hecho aquí. Creo que es emocionante para todos", dijo en la previa del partido un Enzo Maresca que, también en el Chelsea, evitó que el PSG y Luis Enrique levantasen un 'septete' inédito gracias a su triunfo en la final del Mundial de Clubes 2025. En cualquier caso, es consciente de que necesitan "mejorar muchas cosas" para que su Manchester City vuelva a asentarse entre los grandes favoritos para ganar la Champions. "Creo que, sin duda, somos un buen equipo. ¿Dónde estamos en este momento en comparación con el PSG? No lo sé, para ser honesto. Sé lo buenos que son porque han ganado las dos últimas ediciones". Luis Enrique, por su puesto, tendrá ganas de revancha por lo sucedido en Estados Unidos hace dos años... aunque decidió mantenerse al margen respecto a la polémica que rodea al conjunto 'cityzen'. "Tenemos que esperar la decisión final, pero espero que todo salgo bien para el City porque todo lo que han hecho en el campo ha sido increíble". Pocas veces como aquella se vio al PSG de Luis Enrique tan superado desde el punto de vista táctico. Maresca le ganó la partida... y sabe que la de esta noche será la primera gran prueba de la temporada en su objetivo por igualar las tres Champions consecutivas del Real Madrid. "Están en un gran momento y tienen un entrenador con ideas claras. Es un reto motivar". Lo de hoy en el Etihad será un auténtico 'choque de jeques'.

articles.title: Betis - Oporto: horario y dónde ver hoy por TV y 'online' el partido de Champions League
articles.standfirst: Los verdiblancos vuelven a jugar en casa un partido de Liga de Campeones 21 años después
articles.summary: Los verdiblancos vuelven a jugar en casa un partido de Liga de Campeones 21 años después
articles.body: Betis y Oporto se enfrentan este miércoles 14 de octubre en el Estadio de La Cartuja, a partir de las 21.00 horas, en el partido correspondiente a la segunda jornada de la fase de liga de la UEFA Champions League 2026-27. Una cita en la que los verdiblancos buscan su segunda victoria consecutiva en la máxima competición continental ante un conjunto portugués que necesita estrenar su casillero de puntos después de caer en su debut. El equipo de Manuel Pellegrini regresa a la Champions después de estrenarse con un importante triunfo a domicilio frente al Lille francés, un resultado que le permite afrontar su primer compromiso europeo como local de la temporada y en más de 20 años instalado en la zona alta de la clasificación. Lo hace además después de golear por 5-2 a Osasuna el domingo en LaLiga, reforzado anímicamente por su sensacional arranque de temporada. Enfrente estará un Oporto que llega a Sevilla con la necesidad de reaccionar tras perder en la primera jornada ante el Manchester City. El equipo dirigido por Francesco Farioli está arrasando en la liga portuguesa, con pleno de victorias en las ocho primeras jornadas, la última el pasado sábado a domicilio ante el Marítimo por 1-2, pero sucumbió ante los citizens en su estreno continental, por lo que intentará empezar a encauzar cuanto antes su pase a las eliminatorias. El partido entre Betis y Oporto, correspondiente a la segunda jornada de la fase de liga de la UEFA Champions League, se disputa este miércoles 14 de octubre de 2026, a partir de las 21.00 horas, en el Estadio de La Cartuja de Sevilla. El encuentro entre Betis y Oporto se podrá seguir en directo por televisión a través del canal Movistar Liga de Campeones 2, disponible en las plataformas Movistar+ y Orange TV. Además, los aficionados podrán seguir todo lo que suceda en el encuentro a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com, donde también encontrarán la previa, las alineaciones, la crónica y todas las reacciones posteriores al partido. El Betis llega al partido frente al Oporto después de imponerse por 2-3 al Lille en Francia en la primera jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions League. Los verdiblancos ocupan la 11ª posición de la clasificación con tres puntos, dentro de los ocho primeros puestos que dan acceso directo a octavos de final. El Oporto llega al partido frente al Betis después de perder por 0-2 ante el Manchester City en el Estádio do Dragão en la primera jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions League. articles.title: Real Madrid y Roma se conocieron en Caracas
articles.standfirst: Su primer enfrentamiento fue en la quinta edición de la Pequeña Copa del Mundo de Clubes
articles.summary: Su primer enfrentamiento fue en la quinta edición de la Pequeña Copa del Mundo de Clubes
articles.body: La rivalidad entre Real Madrid y Roma no nació en Europa. Hay que viajar hasta Caracas y al verano de 1956 para encontrar el primer rastro de un duelo que esta noche vive su capítulo número once en la Copa de Europa, una saga que se abrió un día ya inscrito en la historia universal: el 11-S, el 11 de septiembre de 2001. Romanos y madrileños cruzaron armas por primera vez en el Olímpico de Caracas. Era la quinta edición de lo que se conoció como la Pequeña Copa del Mundo, cuyo primer ganador fue el Real Madrid en 1952. Para los venezolanos, sin embargo, el torneo tenía otro nombre: Copa Presidente de la República, en honor al dictador Marcos Pérez Jiménez. El equipo blanco regresaba a aquella competición después de que el fútbol español hubiera estado representado por Espanyol, Barcelona y Valencia en las tres ediciones anteriores. El formato era una liguilla a doble vuelta. La edición de 1956 reunió a cuatro equipos: Real Madrid, Vasco da Gama, Oporto y Roma. Organizada por la empresa Van Heusen, la quiniela llegó a Venezuela acompañada de su lema publicitario: “Con el cuello Century, una camisa Van Heusen jamás se arruga”. Los patrocinadores fueron Ron Santa Teresa, Cigarrillos Sport y Sangría Chamberí. El empresario Damián Gaubeka, presidente del comité organizador, contrató para el torneo a dos árbitros argentinos: Lires López y Cuezzo. La Saeta era el gran reclamo. La gran estrella mundial. El Madrid, que el 13 de junio había ganado su primera Copa de Europa, el rival a batir. El Madrid puso rumbo a Caracas a las 8.30 horas del jueves 28 de junio. Dos días antes, Alfredo Di Stéfano acababa el curso de preparadores de la Federación Castellana como el número uno de esa promoción. “Quién sabe si en el futuro me servirá de algo”, comentaba a la vez que señalaba al equipo que veía como gran rival del Madrid en Caracas: “El Oporto. Los portugueses practican un fútbol más fuerte, más parecido al nuestro”. El torneo arrancó el día 30, con un empate a uno entre Oporto y Roma. Al día siguiente, el Madrid confirmó su condición de favorito al vapulear al Vasco da Gama: 5-2, con dos goles de Di Stéfano. Con la colonia española entregada, el segundo partido, ante la Roma, no debía ser más que otro paso de los blancos al título. Sin embargo, el primer Real Madrid-Roma obligó al Madrid a sudar más de lo esperado. Con Di Stéfano alejado del área rival para echar una mano más cerca de la propia y los italianos llenos de entusiasmo. La victoria acabó del lado español, pero la sensación general fue que hasta el empate se habría quedado corto para el juego desplegado por la Roma. Una semana después, el 12 de julio y en el partido de vuelta, la Roma volvió a ser mejor. Y esta vez ganó: 2-1. A los dos goles de Paolo Pestrin, ambos antes de los veinte minutos, sólo respondió el Madrid con uno de penalti de Molowny. Esa fue la única derrota de los blancos en su segunda aparición en la Pequeña Copa del Mundo. Al partido ante la Roma llegaban con tres victorias en tres partidos. Tras la derrota, derrotaron al Oporto (2-1) y empataron a dos con el Vasco da Gama. El título fue para el equipo blanco. El Madrid fue recibido a lo grande. “Este trofeo que tengo entre mis manos demuestra que no ha sido una aventura el viaje a Caracas”, dijo Villalonga en la fiesta en el frontón Fiesta Alegre, en la calle Marqués de Urquijo. El Madrid exhibía su imagen mundial, el poderío universal que tanto entusiasmaba a Bernabéu. La Roma volvió a casa última del campeonato, pero con una victoria que no olvida.

articles.title: Manasse Kianga swaps Sunday league for Champions League
articles.summary: A former student from Rotherham has climbed the football ladder from the bottom up.
articles.body:
side out against Bundesliga outfit Stuttgart in the Champions League, Rossington Main boss Ben Hunter is analysing what happened the night before in his mid-table team's clash in the ninth tier of English football.

They may be separated by thousands of miles and millions of pounds, but the coaches are united by one player.

Manasse Kianga was living in Rotherham and playing Sunday league football when he helped Doncaster outfit Main to promotion to their current level in 2023.

Three years later, he fired the Slovakian champions into Europe's premier competition after reportedly being promoted from the reserves due to an injury crisis.

South African Kianga, 24, could make his debut in the competition later.

Toure's troops began their Champions League campaign away to French giants Paris St-Germain last month and will also take on the likes of Roma and Inter Milan during the tournament's league phase.

"He came to trial with Rossington and I had a look at him and straight away loved him," recalls a proud Hunter, who remains close to the forward known for his electric pace.

"He was a really great guy as well and always played with a smile on his face."

Kianga, who can play anywhere across the front line, emerged from the bench to score an injury-time winner for Slovan in the third and final round of qualifying for this year's Champions League.

He travelled with the first team to the Parc des Princes but missed out on the matchday squad despite registering two goals and two assists in the opening three matches of their domestic campaign.

More recently, Kianga has played and scored for the Sky Blues' reserves and could be involved in their first home fixture in the tournament's league phase.

Hunter remembers the forward as "very raw" in his early days in South Yorkshire, having moved to Rotherham in around 2017.

The move to Rossington came about through Kianga's brother, Bobby, who briefly represented the club.

"You could see his ability in terms of his speed and physical presence, but he was quite slight," says Hunter.

"He stayed with us and he did really well - a lot of higher up teams were interested in him."

At the time, Kianga was studying business and accounting at Thomas Rotherham College, which also counts Jamie Vardy among its former students.

Chris Walls, the college's assistant principal, remembers Kianga as a "popular and outstanding student and football player" who was overlooked by several professional clubs.

He was part of the college's football academy, which mirrors that of a professional set-up, and was "the best player on the pitch every match", says Walls.

"We took him to England schoolboy trials and he made the last 30 but he couldn't get a passport in time to be in the final squad," recalls the assistant principal.

"We're very proud of him and of the success of the football academy scheme at such a small college in Rotherham."

After spells at clubs higher up the non-league pyramid, Kianga returned to Rossington to play a crucial part in their 2022/23 promotion, all while turning out for Team Sport in the Rotherham and District Sunday Football League.

Former Bradford City and Grimsby Town striker Ross Hannah has fond memories of their partnership at Main.

"Me and him were a real problem for defenders and teams because of the way we complemented each other," says Hannah, who is still playing for the club aged 40.

"It's amazing the journey he has been on."

"There were times when he couldn't drive he used to get lifts," recalls Hannah.

"That's the commitment. Some lads would be like: 'I'm not bothered'.

"We have all spoke about it in the dressing room and we are all buzzing for him."

Difficulties obtaining a permanent work permit meant Kianga had to move back to South Africa in 2024.

Hunter was among those who travelled to court in Bradford to support him in his ultimately unsuccessful attempt to stay in England.

"The world was his oyster, I really believed he could have made it pro in England," he says.

"He went back to South Africa and from there made a journey across Europe and ended up where he is."

articles.title: Villa Park: Is stadium rebuild affecting Aston Villa's performances?
articles.summary: With Villa Park's North Stand currently closed for building work, is the reduced capacity affecting Aston Villa's performances?
articles.body:
The Aston Villa head coach was talking about his team's form amid Villa Park's rebuild.

He had already turned the air blue when describing their defeat to Nottingham Forest last month.

It was a rare moment of candour from the Spaniard with Villa yet to win at home this season after Saturday's 2-2 draw with Brentford.

The North Stand is a shell and currently closed for building work as the club increases the stadium's capacity to over 50,000.

It is part of the club's plan to help Villa bridge the financial gap in the Premier League, but they may have to endure some short-term pain for long-term gain.

Fenerbahce visit on Wednesday as Champions League football returns to Villa Park.

With them is Marcos Asensio, who scored eight goals for Emery's men during a successful loan from Paris St-Germain in 2025 - and a reminder of the swagger Villa used to have at home.

He scored in Saturday's 3-0 win over Rizespor, with Fenerbahce netting 11 goals in their last two games, including an 8-0 victory against Turkish Super Lig strugglers Eyupspor.

That could present a problem for a Villa defence that has kept just one clean sheet this season and been increasingly fallible at home, something Emery knows must improve regardless of the rebuild.

"Our handicap is less supporters for the situation, but the club decided it. It is something to improve us for the future," said the Spaniard.

"We must try to be together and without 7,000 supporters we must push everyone. We must play better football, compete better, be more focused. Those are more important than the stand.

"We are realistic with how we are working, improving. The things are not [good] enough yet, a lot of conversations with the team, meetings, video, practising and each match trying to show and improve."

Villa, though, have lost just once at home in Europe under Emery - against Olympiacos in the Europa Conference League semi final in 2024 - and he ended their wait for silverware by lifting the Europa League in May.

"Over the last few years our home form has been amazing, especially in Europe," said defender Matty Cash. "We need to get back to that.

"I don't want to sound like I am making excuses, because obviously we have to deal with the circumstances and it is really good to make the stand bigger and the stadium bigger, but it is obviously different.

"I am not going to sit here and lie and say it isn't but you have to deal with the circumstances. You can't make excuses. You have to play what is in front of you. When it is done it will be amazing but yeah, at the moment it is a bit different."

Champions Arsenal and Forest have already claimed three points at Villa Park this season, with unbeaten Brentford taking a point.

Nicolas Jackson's equalising goal against the Bees was the first Villa had scored in front of the skeleton that was their North Stand this season.

Yet Villa's home struggles are not new. Since the turn of the year they have lost the aura of invincibility which Emery has brought since his arrival almost four years ago.

Between November 2022 and January 2026, they lost just eight of 61 home Premier League games, winning 44 of them.

That included 15 straight wins between March 2023 and December 2023.

They also went 12 months unbeaten in the top flight between August 2024 and August 2025, but since the turn of the year Villa have been fragile at home in comparison.

Defeats by Everton, Brentford, Chelsea and Tottenham threatened their top-four place last season, with Villa needing late goals to earn a draw against Leeds and claim victories against Brighton and Sunderland.

That has continued this season with Villa Park's capacity down to around 37,000 in the void left by the North Stand, something Brentford boss Keith Andrews picked up on, saying he hated playing when one stand was missing.

Villa could still make light of it in Europe, though, with Viking also travelling to Birmingham in the league phase on 21 October.

After an opening win at Club Brugge, successive victories would put them on course for qualification before November, despite their home issues.

"It is a massive test against a good team but we need to be winning these games," added Cash.

"That is the bar we have set for ourselves. Hopefully we can make it loud - three-stand loud."

articles.title: 🚨 Inter and Napoli, double Champions League blow: how good is Serie A? ⚠️
articles.summary: First and second in last season’s Serie A. The two teams that, just a few months ago, were looking down on everyone else. And today, both are still stuck on...
articles.body:
First and second in last season's Serie A. The two teams that, just a few months ago, were looking down on everyone else. And today, both are still stuck on zero points in the Champions League.

Inter and Napoli crumble against Club Bruges and Villarreal, sending a warning that Italian football would do well not to ignore.

Four against Club Bruges at San Siro, three against Villarreal at the Ceramica. The teams conceding them were Inter and Napoli, respectively first and second in last season's Serie A, which the Nerazzurri won with 87 points, ahead of the Azzurri on 76.

The problem, of course, cannot be reduced to a single evening. But that is precisely why this Champions League night has caused such a stir.

Because we are not talking about just any two Italian teams. We are talking about the two sides that best represented the pinnacle of our league last season. And who, as soon as they stepped beyond Serie A, suddenly found themselves far more vulnerable.

Inter concede four to Bruges at San Siro

The most shocking result comes from Milan. Inter 3, Club Bruges 4. Not at the Bernabeu, Anfield or Camp Nou. At San Siro, against a team coming off a home defeat in their opening European fixture.

Nicolò Tresoldi was the undisputed star, scoring a hat-trick. Bruges took the lead from the penalty spot, Lautaro Martinez equalised, and then a mix-up between Josep Martinez and the Inter defence allowed the visitors to go straight back in front.

Tresoldi completed his hat-trick in the second half, Lautaro brought Inter back into the game once again, but Vermant made it 4-2 before Bonny's consolation goal in stoppage time.

Seven goals, plenty of entertainment. But above all, four goals conceded by Inter at home. And that is the figure that should cause concern.

Because the Italian champions showed a fragility that is immediately punished in Europe: individual errors, space in behind, poor defensive judgement and the constant feeling that Bruges could hurt them whenever they beat the initial press.

Inter did respond in attack. But in the Champions League, you cannot expect to have to score five goals to win a home game against Club Bruges.

Napoli: from taking the lead to falling apart

If anything, Napoli's evening tells an even more frustrating story. Because the Azzurri started well at Villarreal. Rrahmani scored after just eight minutes. Hojlund hit the woodwork and came close to making it 2-0.

A mistake by Politano opened the door for Mikautadze to make it 1-1. A minute later, Mourino made it 2-1 with a shot from around thirty metres out. In next to no time, Napoli went from having a chance to double their lead to finding themselves behind. They tried to respond in the second half, but never really managed to shift the momentum of the game, and late on Oluwaseyi made it 3-1 to put the result beyond doubt.

Here too, the score tells only part of the story. Because Napoli had chances. They had positive spells. But Europe does not forgive lapses in concentration.

Is the problem really just Inter and Napoli?

Be careful about turning two matches into a definitive verdict on Italian football. That would be too easy. Anyone can have a bad night, and the Champions League has shown countless times that it can overturn the established order and defy predictions.

But ignoring what happened would be just as superficial. Because Bruges and Villarreal troubled last season's two best Italian teams in very similar ways.

Tempo. Intensity. Directness. Aggression in transition.

When the games opened up, both Inter and Napoli looked far less comfortable than they usually do in Serie A. And perhaps this is where we need to look beyond the scoreline.

Inter and Napoli set the standard in Serie A. The former dominated the league, finishing with 89 goals scored and claiming the 21st Scudetto in their history. Napoli finished immediately behind them.

A few months later, however, Europe presents a very different reckoning. Not against two powerhouses. Against Club Bruges and Villarreal. And so the question becomes unavoidable.

What is being the best in Italy worth today once you step beyond Serie A?

If the top two teams in our league are put under such severe pressure even by opponents outside Europe's very top tier, the problem deserves at least some scrutiny.

Zero points and seven goals: a warning sign

It is not yet time to point fingers. The Champions League is a long campaign, and both Inter and Napoli have enough quality, experience and players to get themselves back in contention. But after two matchdays, the numbers are still there.

Inter: zero points. Napoli: zero points.

And on the same night, last season's top two Serie A sides conceded seven goals between them against Bruges and Villarreal. Perhaps it will turn out to be nothing more than a bad October evening.

But there is another possibility. That this Champions League is holding up a mirror to Italian football that makes for uncomfortable viewing. Because dominating Serie A is one thing. Trying to do the same when the tempo rises to European levels is, evidently, a whole different story.

articles.title: Liverpool and Chelsea hopes raised as rivals change stance over £100m star
articles.summary: Alex Scott to Liverpool? Bournemouth Set £100m January Valuation Amid Transfer InterestBournemouth are prepared to consider the sale of Alex Scott in January...
articles.body:
Alex Scott to Liverpool? Bournemouth Set £100m January Valuation Amid Transfer Interest

Bournemouth are prepared to consider the sale of Alex Scott in January, although any deal would depend on two major conditions being met. As Metro first reported, the south coast club would only entertain an exit if an offer in the region of £100 million arrives and their Premier League position provides enough comfort to proceed.

That stance reflects Scott's growing importance and his rising profile in English football. The 23-year-old enjoyed his strongest top-flight campaign last season and has since taken another step forward by breaking into the senior England set-up under Thomas Tuchel. His first two caps appear to have further underlined why leading clubs continue to monitor him so closely.

Liverpool and Chelsea retain Alex Scott interest

Liverpool and Chelsea were both linked heavily with Scott during the summer and those connections have not disappeared. Liverpool's interest carries an obvious layer given Andoni Iraola is now head coach at Anfield after previously working with Scott at Bournemouth. The midfielder's tactical flexibility, energy and ability to carry possession through central areas are qualities that would make sense for a number of elite sides.

Chelsea, meanwhile, are also credited with strong interest as they assess midfield options following Enzo Fernandez's move to Manchester City. Scott has long been viewed as one of the most technically gifted young midfielders in the country, and there is a growing sense that Bournemouth may eventually have to make a decision on his future.

Bournemouth stance shaped by contract and league position

Bournemouth were not willing to sanction a departure after last season, particularly after Scott's influence became clearer across the campaign. Even so, his current contract situation remains part of the wider picture. He is tied down until 2028 on the terms agreed when he joined from Bristol City in 2023, but reports indicate he has already turned down proposals to extend that deal.

There have now been fresh discussions between the club and the player's camp, with Bournemouth understood to be more open to a potential January sale. That does not mean an exit is likely at any cost. Much will rest on results over the coming months.

Marco Rose has endured a difficult beginning, with Bournemouth still chasing a first Premier League win and sitting on three points from six matches. If the club remain concerned about the threat of relegation, keeping Scott could become a football decision before a financial one.

Injury setback complicates January picture

Scott's immediate focus is recovery after suffering a quad injury on England duty. The issue is expected to sideline him for around a month, denying Bournemouth one of their key midfielders during an important stretch of fixtures.

Rose said: "It's an injury from a muscle, and we'll do pictures [scans] in some days again. But we're going to miss him, for sure, for four or five weeks. I'm very disappointed and it's a big loss.

"We miss a very important player, but I don't want to blame anyone."We are very happy that he made his debut for the English national team. He did well and we just hope that he is getting fit again quite soon."

For now, Bournemouth hold the cards. Liverpool interest, Chelsea interest and Alex Scott's own trajectory all point towards a major future move. The question is whether January becomes the moment, and whether anyone is ready to meet a £100 million valuation.

From a Liverpool perspective, this is the kind of report that will naturally spark excitement. Scott looks like a player with the mobility, intensity and technical level to fit into a modern, aggressive midfield. He can receive under pressure, drive forward and play with purpose, which are all attributes supporters tend to value highly.

The obvious pull is Andoni Iraola. If a coach already knows the player, trusts his character and understands how to deploy him, that always matters. Liverpool's recruitment has often looked strongest when there is absolute clarity on role and profile, and Scott appears to tick plenty of boxes in that regard.

That said, £100 million feels enormous, especially for a January deal and especially with Bournemouth likely to dig in if results stay poor. Liverpool supporters will probably admire the player while also wondering whether that fee could be better spread across multiple positions.

Still, if Scott keeps progressing at this rate, the price may only keep climbing. For a hopeful Liverpool fan, the ideal scenario is simple, monitor the situation closely, maintain the relationship, and be ready if Bournemouth soften their stance. If Iraola truly sees him as a major piece for the next phase at Anfield, supporters will trust that judgment and hope the club are in position to act decisively.

articles.title: Stamford Bridge hosting Shakhtar’s Champions League matches, starting tonight
articles.summary: Potential rooting interest
articles.body:
Chelsea and Shakhtar Donetsk struck a deal earlier this year to stage the latter's Champions League matches at Stamford Bridge this season, giving the nomadic team from the war-torn region (since 2014) in Ukraine a proper European home, at least temporarily. It's an especially appropriate arrangement given Chelsea's former ties to Roman Abramovich.

"At this point we are not representing just Shakhtar Donetsk. We are representing the whole country. For us, it's also to support Ukrainian people who left their homes and moved to London, to England. And therefore, these games completely change context. It's very important every time to send messages to support Ukraine." -Sergei Palkin, Shakhtar CEO; source: Politico

"At this point we are not representing just Shakhtar Donetsk. We are representing the whole country. For us, it's also to support Ukrainian people who left their homes and moved to London, to England. And therefore, these games completely change context. It's very important every time to send messages to support Ukraine."

Sergei Palkin, Shakhtar CEO; source: Politico

The first of (at least) four games that Shakhtar will play at the Bridge is tonight, as they take on Greek Super League champions AEK Athens. The other three games will be against Sporting CP (including Chelsea loanee Jesse Derry) on November 3, Fenerbahçe (including N'Golo Kanté, Romelu Lukaku, and Nathan Aké) on November 25, and Real Madrid (including Marc Cucurella, Antonio Rüdiger, Thibaut Courtois, and, should he still be there by then, José Mourinho) on January 27. A nice slate of matches for West London.

Date / Time: Wednesday, October 14, 2026, 20.00 BST; 3pm EDT How to watch: TNT Sports 8 / HBO Max (UK); Paramount+ (USA); elsewhere

Chelsea are only running logistics for these events, with all ticketing handled by Shakhtar. That said, there are tickets still available for tonight's game (not just hospitality), for example, so it shouldn't be too hard to go if you are interested, able, and willing. European nights at the Bridge are still European nights, especially at slightly reduced prices compared to the normal fares.

Shakhtar are currently managed by the legendary Arda Turan, and feature a number of Brazilian talents as usual. Any new Willians among them?

articles.title: Lisandro Martinez: Jamie Carragher says Man Utd defender's comments criticising hierarchy are awful as Wayne Rooney brands them disrespectful
articles.summary: After Man Utd's 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid, Lisandro Martinez had expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox; Man Utd spent £155m on just four major summer signings after a third-place Premier League finish last season
articles.body:
In an astonishing post-match interview after United's 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid with 10 men, defender Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club chiefs, critisicing the lack of summer investment in the squad.

Martinez - who is out of contract at the end of the season - said he expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox, in the most recent transfer window in which they failed to improve their options at left-back and up front.

And responding to those comments, Sky Sports pundit Carragher told CBS Sports: "It doesn't do anybody any good at all, and they will be the story now for the next few days all about this.

"Every set of supporters don't like the suits or the guys upstairs, so United fans will lap this up and think it's great. I think it's awful that he's come out and said that right now. I do.

"And when he's saying 'we had a fantastic season last season', they didn't. A manager got sacked last season. Sacked.

"They finished third because they had no cup games. They got knocked out of the cup competitions very early. The reason they finished third is Liverpool and Chelsea were that bad as well.

"Now we're seeing the real Manchester United this season. They were awful again tonight.

"And him as well, when he's talking at the start of this season - I think he's a good player, by the way, he's a World Cup winner, I get that - he's had an awful start to the season. Awful. Really poor.

"And yeah, people are lapping it up, Manchester United fans will. That does nobody any good at all."

Man Utd spent £155m on just four major summer signings after a third-place Premier League finish last season, which earned a return to the Champions League for the first time in three years.

But Martinez is not happy with how the club navigated the summer.

"I have to control myself a lot, but sometimes it's a reflection of how our club is at the moment," Martinez told Amazon Prime .

"We had a fantastic season last season, and now we expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete because many teams have brought in many players as well."

Asked whether he had expected more investment in the squad in summer, Martinez said: "Yes, 100 per cent.

"I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest. And also, as a player, we have to do more.

"It's also important to build a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

Tuesday's loss in Madrid extended Man Utd's winless run to five games, piling pressure on boss Michael Carrick.

"He does his best," he said of Carrick. "But every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season.

"The teams know how you play, they know every detail. If you don't change, next season is a big problem."

Asked about Carrick's future, Martinez replied: "You start changing, changing, changing managers. But what about [moves his eyes upwards] other areas?"

Martinez looked up and then shrugged, saying, "I can't say more" before deciding to add a final dig.

"Because also tonight it is easy to say the coach, it is easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas," he said, pointing up and nodding.

Rooney: Martinez has gone too far, his performances aren't good enough

Martinez's comments also drew criticism from former Manchester United captain Wayne Rooney, who agreed with Carragher that the Argentina defender's performances have not been good enough to make such an outburst.

Rooney also feels Martinez's comments are disrespectful to the other United players.

"It's a difficult one because I always used to think I was outspoken as a player and you want to have your opinion," Rooney told Amazon Prime.

"I think he has maybe gone a bit too far. That's for the manager, and that should really stay internal.

"The fans want to hear the players speak; they want to hear the players care, so you can clearly see he cares and he wants the team to invest more money, and more players, and to do that he is probably one of the players who is out the door through his performances. His performances haven't been good enough.

"But I think in some ways he is right in terms of the club needs to invest more, at the top end of the pitch and in defence as well.

"But it looks like that was a bit of an agenda; he's wanted to say that, because that doesn't mirror the performance. I thought the performance was better.

"It's a bit disrespectful to his team-mates as well. He is disrespecting his team-mates because he's saying the team isn't good enough.

"Bruno (Fernandes) is the only one who has any right to come out and say anything like that as captain. And even then it should be behind closed doors if there are issues, which does happen.

"Players have conversations with the manager, the manager has conversations with the board, but that interview is not going to help the situation the club are in at the minute.

"That's going to bring a greater noise around it; the players are not happy, they're not settled, they don't trust in their team-mates. That's not going to help at all."

articles.standfirst: El conjunto azulón no estará solo en el Estadio Ion Oblemenco para su debut en Conference League
articles.summary: El conjunto azulón no estará solo en el Estadio Ion Oblemenco para su debut en Conference League
articles.body: El Getafe no estará solo en Craiova. La afición getafense se desplazará este jueves al Estadio Ion Oblemenco para el encuentro que disputará el conjunto azulón frente al Universitatea Craiova correspondiente a la Fase Liga de la UEFA Conference League. Los de José Bordalás tendrán el aliento de más de 300 hinchas que se liaron la manta a la cabeza y, pese a ser un día laborable, no han querido perderse el regreso a una competición europea de los suyos seis años después. El equipo, que logró deshacerse del Partizan de Belgrado en la previa, saborea ya una nueva aventura por el viejo continente que lo lleva a Rumanía en esta primera parada. El futbolista del Getafe, Ramón Terrats, señaló para Marca que el equipo agradece el apoyo de la hinchada y destacó “el esfuerzo que supone”, tanto en tiempo como en dinero, el desplazamiento de la hinchada desplazada. “Solo podemos darles las gracias, porque sentimos su apoyo y nos hacen notar que, incluso cuando jugamos fuera de casa, no estamos solos”, continuó. Además, el futbolista hizo hincapié en la iniciativa del club, que regalará la entrada a todos los aficionados que viajen al feudo rumano, algo que para el mediocentro sirve para “fortalecer” el vínculo entre “el equipo” y la afición y “demostrar” que ambos van en “la misma dirección”. "Sabemos que el club y la afición del Getafe están muy unidos. En un equipo como el nuestro, eso es fundamental, porque no somos uno de los grandes, especialmente en el aspecto económico. Para seguir creciendo y conseguir cosas importantes, necesitamos que todos rememos en la misma dirección. El esfuerzo de cada uno, dentro y fuera del campo, es clave. Si cada parte mira solo por sí misma, será mucho más difícil alcanzar objetivos bonitos juntos", dijo. Terrats además señaló que el equipo está “ilusionado” con esta nueva aventura europea. El ex del Espanyol destacó que “jugar la Conference League es un plus, una recompensa al trabajo que hizo el equipo la temporada pasada, tanto de los que siguen como de los que ya no están”. “Nosotros también nos la hemos ganado superando la previa y ahora queremos disfrutarla al máximo. Sabemos que, además, puede ser importante para el club a nivel económico si conseguimos avanzar rondas, así que todos salimos beneficiados de esta aventura en la Conference", sentenció.

articles.title: Los Al-Thani reaccionan y contratan al abogado de Cristiano Ronaldo para su hijo Rakan
articles.standfirst: Rakan no contaba con un abogado particular y tuvo que afrontar los acontecimientos de la pasada semana en los juzgados de Madrid y Málaga con una letrada de oficio
articles.summary: Rakan no contaba con un abogado particular y tuvo que afrontar los acontecimientos de la pasada semana en los juzgados de Madrid y Málaga con una letrada de oficio
articles.body: La detención de Rakan Al-Thani parece haber provocado un movimiento en la familia catarí. Después de años de silencio y de permanecer prácticamente al margen de la situación judicial que afecta al clan, Abdullah Al-Thani ha dado un paso para defender a su hijo. Los Al-Thani han recurrido a un abogado de primer nivel para tratar de sacar a Rakan de prisión. Se trata de Javier Velasco Almendral, del bufete de Javier Choclán, uno de los despachos más reconocidos del país y que ha representado en importantes procedimientos a figuras como Cristiano Ronaldo o Julio Iglesias. Hasta ahora, Rakan no contaba con un abogado particular y tuvo que afrontar los acontecimientos de la pasada semana en los juzgados de Madrid y Málaga con una letrada de oficio. La llegada de Velasco cambia el escenario. Su principal objetivo pasa por conseguir que Rakan abandone Soto del Real, donde permanece en prisión provisional desde la noche del pasado jueves. La defensa también reclama poder ratificar el apoderamiento del acusado y que todas las resoluciones judiciales que le afecten sean comunicadas con la asistencia de un intérprete de árabe. El movimiento supone, al menos, un cambio de estrategia por parte de los Al-Thani. El silencio había sido la tónica de Abdullah desde 2020, pero la situación de su hijo parece haber obligado a la familia a tomar cartas en el asunto. Aunque el jeque no se ha pronunciado públicamente sobre la detención y posterior ingreso en prisión de Rakan, la contratación de Velasco evidencia que está al tanto de lo que está ocurriendo y que existe interés por actuar en el frente judicial. Velasco, eso sí, no pudo ejercer todavía como abogado de Rakan durante su comparecencia en Madrid. El hijo de Abdullah ya le había otorgado poderes mientras permanecía detenido en Alemania. Según el escrito incorporado al procedimiento y al que ha tenido acceso 'ABC', Rakan firmó el 15 de septiembre en la prisión de Landshut un documento bilingüe de apoderamiento, al no poder comparecer ante un notario español ni ante el Letrado de la Administración de Justicia. Sobre el clan Al-Thani pesa una petición de la Fiscalía de 14 años y medio de prisión para Rakan, sus hermanos Nasser y Nayef y su padre Abdullah por delitos de apropiación indebida, administración desleal e imposición de acuerdos abusivos. Mientras tanto, Abdullah mantiene su silencio sobre la situación de su hijo. En sus últimos mensajes en redes sociales no ha hecho ninguna referencia a Rakan. Su última publicación hablaba de "apariencias", acusaciones y la necesidad de someter los registros a un examen independiente. Un tipo de mensaje que el jeque viene utilizando de forma recurrente durante los últimos años y que, por su carácter prediseñado, se ha convertido prácticamente en una constante en sus redes sociales.

articles.title: Samu se prepara para debutar en la Champios ante el Betis y la ciudad donde se crió: "Ojalá sea un gran día"
articles.standfirst: El internacional español nacido en Melilla pasó su infancia en Sevilla y jugó en el Nervión
articles.summary: El internacional español nacido en Melilla pasó su infancia en Sevilla y jugó en el Nervión
articles.body: El delantero español del Oporto, Samu Aghehowa, nacido en Melilla y criado en Sevilla, calificó como "un partido especial" el de la visita este miércoles al Betis, en la segunda jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions League, y afirmó que "ojalá sea un gran día no sólo" para él, "sino también para su equipo". El internacional absoluto por España, de 22 años y de origen nigeriano, manifestó este martes en la rueda de prensa previa en el Estadio La Cartuja que, por encima de la connotación "especial" de este encuentro por sus vivencias en la capital andaluza, el Oporto llega a Sevilla "con un objetivo: ganar". "Lo más importante es ayudar al equipo, ya sea con goles o con mi trabajo", recalcó el delantero del campeón portugués, que podría debutar frente al Betis en la máxima competición europea, a la que el Oporto llega después de su derrota en casa ante el Manchester City inglés (0-2), con un doblete del noruego Erling Haland en la primera jornada. El melillense incidió en que "volver a Sevilla siempre es especial", ya que ha "pasado la mayor parte" de su vida "aquí", puesto que se formó en la AD Nervión antes de pasar al Granada y luego al Atlético de Madrid, que lo cedió al Alavés en la campaña 2023-24. "Poder debutar en la 'Champions' aquí es una de esas coincidencias de la vida, pero ojalá mañana sea un gran día no solo para mí, sino también para el equipo", subrayó Samu, quien aseguró que, tras varios meses de baja por su lesión el pasado febrero en el ligamento cruzado anterior, "lo más importante" es sentirse "bien en los entrenamientos y en los partidos". Añadió que, "al final, éste es el camino" que le llevará a lo que más le "gusta: marcar goles" y vaticinó que "pronto" volverá a marcar, al tiempo que aseveró que durante su largo periodo de recuperación, después de su grave lesión de rodilla, ha trabajado "más duro que nunca". "Lo sacrifiqué todo para estar aquí y me siento mejor que antes. No tengo miedo. La lesión es cosa del pasado y estoy preparado para lo que venga. Me siento genial y muy feliz de volver a jugar", indicó el delantero del Oporto. Admitió que, cuando supo que se enfrentaría al equipo verdiblanco en Sevilla, "enseguida" le escribió a sus amigos, "muchos de los cuales son hinchas del Betis, y también" a su familia, de la que dijo que, "por fin", podrá verle "debutar en la Liga de Campeones". "Pedí algunas entradas, claro... -señaló entre risas-, pero hay sitio para todos", comentó el internacional español, quien elogió al Betis, un club que "ha crecido mucho en los últimos años y está rindiendo muy bien en LaLiga", por lo que "no será un partido fácil porque tienen jugadores de gran nivel". "Lo más importante es que nosotros hagamos lo que sabemos hacer", dijo Samu, y agregó sobre el capitán bético Isco Alarcón que coincidió "con él una vez en la selección nacional y es un jugador con mucho talento", pero incidió en que el Oporto también tiene "un gran equipo" y que necesitan "concentrarse" en sí mismos y "jugar un buen partido".

articles.title: Abelardo alerta al Barcelona de lo que "le falta" para ganar la Champions: "Un central de garantías"
articles.summary: Abelardo alerta al Barcelona de lo que "le falta" para poder ganar la Champions: "Un central de garantías"
articles.body: Abelardo alerta al Barcelona de lo que "le falta" para poder ganar la Champions: "Un central de garantías" 'El Pitu' Abelardo, jugador del F.C. Barcelona de 1994 a 2002, analizó en el programa 'Radioestadio Noche' de Onda Cero las opciones que tiene un lanzado F.C Barcelona de ganar la Champions League. "Ojalá me equivoque pero para ganar la Champions creo que al Barça le falta algo atrás, un central de garantías", comentó en Onda Cero el exfutbolista 56 años, que como entrenador ha dirigido a Sporting B, Candás, Tuilla, Alavés, Espanyol, Sporting y Cartagena. Abelardo destacó el partidazo de Lamine Yamal en la remontada del Barcelona ante el Galatasaray en Champions League, en un partido que acabó ganando 1-4: "Yo no sé si es el mejor tiempo que le he visto a Lamine Yamal en su carrera, pero de los mejores. O sea, ha hecho un segundo tiempo para enmarcar. En todas las jugadas de ataque ha parecido él, con una calidad, unos pases extraordinarios, en el gol que mete Gordon hace una rabona que se hace un autopase de rabona queriendo. Bueno, ha estado sublime, o sea, parecía Messi en vez de Lamine Yama. Ha estado increíble". El exfutbolista, que fue 54 veces internacional con España, destacó que "si Lamine Yamal juega a ese nivel el Barça es imparable. Lo veo increíblemente bien, es el mejor equipo de Europa". "Yo creo que para aspirar a ganar la Champions League a Barcelona le falta un central de nivel. Para mí sí... ojalá me equivoque". Abelardo destacó que contra el Galatasaray "por centímetro los turcos no se van con un 2-0". "Al final vas a tener que ganar duelos en defensa con Kvaratskhelia, Harry Kane... Yo creo que el Barça, atrás, le falta todavía, para mí, jugadores de primer nivel para poder aspirar a ganar la Champions, que la puede ganar, pero yo creo que todavía le falta", subrayó.
